projects.name: Fetch PHP
projects.description: Modern PHP HTTP client inspired by JavaScript's fetch API. Async/await, streaming, SSE, middleware, RFC 7234 caching, and full PSR-7/18 compliance.
readmeExcerpt: Fetch PHP is a Guzzle-based HTTP client for PHP with a small global fetch() helper, an object-oriented client, PSR-7 and PSR-18 support, streaming, middleware, retries, and optional caching.
The API takes inspiration from JavaScript Fetch. It uses PHP values and Guzzle request options, and it does not implement the browser Fetch API or its security model.
Runtime packages: Guzzle 7.9+, PSR-7 1.x/2.x, PSR-3 1.x/2.x/3.x, ReactPHP event-loop and promise packages, and jerome/matrix ^4.0

projects.name: Filterable
projects.description: Enhance Laravel queries with adaptable, customisable filters and intelligent caching to improve both performance and functionality.
readmeExcerpt: Filterable turns HTTP request parameters into explicit, reusable Eloquent query filters. Declare handlers with attributes or existing properties, then opt into validation, transformations, permissions, caching, complexity limits, logging, optimization, streaming, and query chaining.

This README is the complete usage guide. Examples below use an application Post model with ordinary fields such as title , body , status , price , is available , published at , and tenant id ; adapt those names and relationships to your schema.
Registering filters: attributes, properties, and aliases

projects.name: phpvm
projects.description: Simple PHP version manager for MacOS and Linux.
readmeExcerpt: phpvm is a lightweight PHP Version Manager that allows you to easily install, switch between, and manage multiple PHP versions via the command line.

Seamlessly switch between installed PHP versions. Run commands with a specific PHP version without globally switching ( phpvm exec , phpvm run ). List available remote PHP versions from your system package manager ( phpvm ls-remote ). Install the latest available remote PHP version with phpvm install latest-remote . Update phpvm in place using phpvm self-update to pull the latest stable script version. Resolve ver…

Auto-switch PHP versions based on project .phpvmrc (configurable depth via PHPVM PHPVMRC MAX DEPTH ). Composer-aware version detection — phpvm use , phpvm install , and phpvm resolve read the PHP requirement from composer.json ( config.platform.php or require.php ) when no version is given.

projects.name: Honeymelon
projects.description: Honeymelon - free, open-source desktop media conversion for video, audio and images. Local processing, no account or uploads.
readmeExcerpt: Previously Comet. The next desktop build is 3.0.0-beta.2 ; published legacy releases retain their original names, filenames and checksums.
A compact desktop app for converting video, audio, and images. Choose your files, pick an output format, and convert them locally with bundled media tools.
No account, upload, or cloud processing is required.

projects.name: Matrix
projects.description: Event-driven async helpers for ReactPHP with promise composition, cancellation, timeouts, concurrency limits, and rate limiting.
readmeExcerpt: Matrix provides event-driven async helpers for ReactPHP: promise composition, concurrency limits, retries, timeouts, cancellation, rate limiting, events, and metrics. Work runs cooperatively on one event loop; callbacks must use nonblocking I/O.
This README is the repository's documentation, including the API reference, migration guide, and release history.
Matrix requires PHP 8.3 or newer, react/event-loop ^1.6, and react/promise ^3.3. Composer installs the ReactPHP dependencies. The pcntl , posix , and sockets extensions are optional.

projects.name: Dokimos
projects.description: CLI for plagiarism evidence discovery and AI-writing-risk analysis
readmeExcerpt: Dokimos discovers plagiarism evidence from free remote sources, optionally checks a local indexed corpus, and scores documents for AI-likeness using stylometric heuristics.
The Python distribution name is still dokimos-cli , but the primary command is dokimos .
